about: Public SQLite sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 documentation (https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/wal_checkpoint_v2.html), reviewed 2026-11-15. Condensed source context distinguishes PASSIVE from RESTART and checkpoint-lock contention. A new completed report generalized a secondary source's no-busy-handler statement to all checkpoints; the decisive API page was not retrieved. This case tests interpretation when that context is supplied, not search coverage.

findings.title: Checkpoint a database - SQLite C Interface
findings.content: Checkpoint behavior depends on mode and lock type. SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE: The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode. SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART: after checkpointing, it blocks (calls the busy-handler callback) until readers no longer need the WAL. A conflicting checkpoint lock returns SQLITE_BUSY without calling a configured busy handler; this exception does not remove the busy handler from RESTART's wait for readers.

claims.claim: SQLite never invokes the busy handler during checkpoint operations, including RESTART while waiting for readers.
SQLite PASSIVE checkpoint mode does not invoke the busy handler.
SQLite RESTART checkpoint mode invokes the busy handler while waiting for readers after checkpointing.
